mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-38.9 to -37.1 to -38.0 to -35.7), indicating a steady recovery in discretionary outings. This momentum should persist, pushing the 4-week forward mean of RETAIL_REC above the trailing 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -38.9 to -35.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If the forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the trailing 28-day mean despite the recent uptrend, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has stayed in a narrow band around -30 to -31.6 for four weeks, showing no clear recovery in commuting-linked travel. If TRANSIT crosses above -28 (a 2+ point weekly improvement), it signals renewed mobility that should lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks as transit-dependent shoppers return to stores.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -28 week-on-week (a gain of at least 2 points from -30.0)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT range -31.6 to -30.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses the threshold but RETAIL_REC's forward mean does not exceed its trailing mean within two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PARKS mobility (3.0 to 14.4 over four weeks) combined with stable-to-slightly-declining RESIDENTIAL (7.4 to 6.1) suggests households are substituting outdoor leisure for home confinement. When both trends co-occur, discretionary retail trips tend to rise jointly with outdoor activity, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises while RESIDENTIAL falls or stays flat for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 3.0 to 14.4 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 7.4 to 6.1
failure_condition: If PARKS continues rising and RESIDENTIAL continues falling but RETAIL_REC's forward mean does not exceed its trailing mean, the joint-substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-August in Manhattan reflects peak summer seasonal outdoor activity (PARKS at 14.4, highest of the series). As this seasonal peak gives way to the end-of-summer transition and eventual school/work resumption in early September, outdoor-substitution effects on retail should fade, causing RETAIL_REC to plateau or decline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached its four-week high of 14.4 at t-0w
regime_hint: summer seasonal peak transitioning to autumn
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean exceeds its trailing mean despite PARKS declining from its seasonal peak, the seasonal-fade hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has remained deeply suppressed and stable near -39 for four consecutive weeks, indicating persistent hybrid/remote-work policies at NYC employers. This structural policy stance caps weekday lunchtime and after-work retail visits, keeping RETAIL_REC from rising meaningfully over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES held between -39.6 and -38.1 for four weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains flat near -39 but RETAIL_REC's forward mean rises meaningfully above its trailing mean, the policy-cap hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM improved sharply from -27.1 to -22.1 in the first two weeks then plateaued near -22.3. If GROCERY_PHARM drops below -25 again (a regression of necessity-trip activity), it would signal renewed caution among residents that also suppresses discretionary retail visits within the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -25 week-on-week from its current -22.4 level
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM plateaued near -22 for the last three weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM crosses below -25 but RETAIL_REC's forward 7-day mean does not fall relative to its trailing mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES have both stayed flat and depressed simultaneously (TRANSIT ~-30, WORKPLACES ~-39) over the last four weeks. Their joint stagnation indicates no new commuter-driven footfall is entering retail corridors; only if both begin to co-improve together will RETAIL_REC see a meaningful lift within two weeks, since commuter-adjacent retail depends on combined transit and office activity.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remained flat over four weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve together for two weeks but RETAIL_REC's forward mean does not rise, the joint commuter-driver hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In the specific regime of a NYC August heatwave period, elevated PARKS usage (14.4) paired with stable RESIDENTIAL (6.1) reflects short-term seasonal outdoor leisure that temporarily substitutes for retail shopping trips, producing a near-term one-week dip in RETAIL_REC before normalizing.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at four-week high of 14.4 with RESIDENTIAL near four-week low of 6.1
failure_condition: If PARKS stays elevated and RESIDENTIAL stays low but RETAIL_REC's next 7-day mean does not fall below the prior week's mean, the seasonal-substitution hypothesis is rejected.
